# Judith Chapter 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_003_page_001.jpg

---

**3:1** The nations sent messengers to him with words of peace, saying:

**3:2** "Behold, we are the servants of Nebuchadnezzar the great king, and we lie prostrate before you. Do with us as seems good to you.

**3:3** Behold, our estates and all our land and all our wheat fields and our flocks and our herds and all the encampments of our tents lie before your face — do with them as you please.

**3:4** Behold, our cities and their inhabitants are also your slaves — come and deal with them as seems good in your eyes."

**3:5** The men came to Holofernes and reported all these words to him.

**3:6** Then he came down to the seacoast with his army, garrisoned the fortified cities, and took from them chosen men as auxiliaries.

**3:7** The people received him and all the surrounding country with garlands and dances and tambourines.

**3:8** He tore down their frontier shrines and cut down their sacred groves, for it had been given to him to destroy all the gods of the land, so that all nations would worship Nebuchadnezzar alone and all their tongues and all their tribes would invoke him as god.

**3:9** Then he came toward Esdraelon, near Dothan, which faces the great ridge of Judea.

**3:10** He encamped between Geba and Scythopolis and remained there a full month, gathering all the supplies of his army.
